history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE: the CSV row 'Khandoba Temple, Aurangabad' is generic - there are several Khandoba temples in and around Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (e.g. at Satara, Kadepathar, Khokadpura). This record is mapped to the prominent Shri Khandoba Temple at Satara (Aurangabad MIDC area, 431005), about 2.7 km from Aurangabad railway station - reclassify if the CSV intends a different shrine. Dedicated to Lord Khandoba (Martanda Bhairava, a form of Shiva), it sits amid hills near Satara village; worship of Khandoba is dated to the 12th-13th century. Sources describe a 12th-century Yadava-era temple rebuilt during the Peshwa reign and renovated in 1766 by Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar; the nave is stone while the spire is brick. It is more than 500 years old and a lively local cultural hub during festivals.

name: Khandoba Temple
town_description: Satara is a village/locality adjoining the MIDC industrial area on the outskirts of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad), about 2.7 km from the railway station, set against scenic low hills. It is primarily known for the hill-set Shri Khandoba Temple. The city itself is the historic Marathwada capital and gateway to the Ajanta and Ellora Caves, with landmarks such as Bibi Ka Maqbara and Daulatabad Fort.
